Write an email to a colleague about being honest when it costs you something. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: On Being Honest When It Costs Us

Dear Mark,

I want to write to you about something that has been on my mind since our meeting last week, and I hope you will take it in the spirit in which it is meant.

You will remember that when the numbers on the Henderson project came in below what we had promised, there was a moment when it would have been very easy to say nothing, or to say just enough to let the matter pass. I noticed that you chose to tell the client plainly what had happened. I know that it cost you something. I know, too, that it was not a pleasant conversation. But I want you to understand that I think it was the best thing you did all quarter.

It is easy enough to be honest when honesty costs us nothing. Any person can tell the truth when the truth is welcome. The real test comes when we must say what is unpleasant, when we must admit a mistake that no one else would ever have discovered, or when we must decline to say a comfortable thing that we do not believe. It is in just such moments that character is built, and it is in just such moments that it is lost.

Now, I do not wish you to think that I am speaking only of the large matters. In my experience it is the small ones that matter most. The man who will shade the truth a little in a report, or let a doubtful figure stand because it looks better, is forming a habit, and the habit will grow. It is better ten times over to take the small loss today than to become the sort of person whom others must check and double-check.

You will find, I think, that people remember these things. The client may have been disappointed for a week, but he will trust your word for years. That kind of trust cannot be bought, and it cannot be borrowed. It must be earned, a little at a time, and very often at some expense to ourselves.

I hope that you will keep going forward in just this way. There is nothing in what has happened to discourage you; there is, on the contrary, a great deal to be proud of.

If you should like to talk the matter over, my door is open at any time this week.

Sincerely,

[name]
